symptomShortText: Chatter marks on rotor shaft ground diameter

causesIshikawa.description: EMP-6033, Shift A - dressing cycle run at the released interval
EQ-GRIND04-001 spindle bearing vibration 7.9 mm/s RMS against a 2.8 mm/s alarm limit; trend rising since 2026-07-20
DOC-9120 Rev C - grinding parameters and dressing interval unchanged
Bar stock hardness 58 HRC within the 56-60 HRC band
Roughness tester GA-0402, last cal 2026-07-11, R&R 4.8%

fiveWhyChain.question: Why are there chatter marks on the ground diameter?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Surface roughness measured 2.8um against a 0.8um maximum and roundness 0.014mm against 0.006mm, the signature of vibration during grinding

fiveWhyChain.question: Why was there vibration during grinding? (root cause)
fiveWhyChain.answer: Spindle bearing vibration reached 7.9 mm/s RMS against a 2.8 mm/s alarm limit, indicating bearing degradation

fiveWhyChain.question: Why did a rising vibration trend since 2026-07-20 not trigger intervention?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Condition monitoring data is reviewed monthly rather than on threshold breach, so the alarm limit was crossed without anyone acting

actions.actionText: Stop WC-GRIND-04, quarantine batch B-53001 and route R60 grinding to WC-GRIND-01
Replace the WC-GRIND-04 spindle bearing set and re-qualify the machine with a capability run

lessonsLearned.whatWorked: Comparing two grinding cells running the same job isolated the machine within one shift
lessonsLearned.whatDidnt: Vibration data was trending toward the limit for two weeks with nobody watching it

isIsNot.isWhereWhenItHappens: R60 shafts ground on WC-GRIND-04 from 2026-08-01 onward
isIsNot.isNotWhereWhenItDoesnt: R60 ground on WC-GRIND-01 - same wheel spec, same bar stock lot
isIsNot.notes: Defect follows the machine, not the material or the wheel

customerReference.complaintReference: N/A - internal defect, no customer reference
